\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{धावणे} (dhāvṇe)}{धावणे (dhāvṇe)}]{\mr{धावणे} (dhāvṇe) — to run}

\label{lesson:MR-C78-dhavne}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for to hear, then the Marathi for to get up.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{धावणे}}
\textbf{\mr{धावणे}} — \emph{dhāvṇe} — \textquotedblleft{}to run\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{धावणे}} (\emph{dhāvṇe}) is a tadbhava, a word inherited from Sanskrit and reshaped by sound change. It comes from \emph{dhāvati}, \textquotedblleft{}runs, flows\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 6802).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dhāvṇe}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marathi for to hear, then the Marathi for to get up, then say \emph{dhāvṇe} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{खेळणे} (kheḷṇe)}{खेळणे (kheḷṇe)}]{\mr{खेळणे} (kheḷṇe) — to play}

Before the new one: say the Marathi for to get up, then the Marathi for to run.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{खेळणे}}
\textbf{\mr{खेळणे}} — \emph{kheḷṇe} — \textquotedblleft{}to play\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{खेळणे}} (\emph{kheḷṇe}) is inherited from a reconstructed \emph{*khēl-}, \textquotedblleft{}play\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 3918). CDIAL links it with Sanskrit \emph{krīḍati}, \textquotedblleft{}plays\textquotedblright{}: if that verb has a non-Aryan source, these forms may share it.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{विकणे} (vikṇe)}{विकणे (vikṇe)}]{\mr{विकणे} (vikṇe) — to sell}

\label{lesson:MR-C78-vikne}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for to run, then the Marathi for to play.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{विकणे}}
\textbf{\mr{विकणे}} — \emph{vikṇe} — \textquotedblleft{}to sell\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{विकणे}} (\emph{vikṇe}) is a tadbhava, a word inherited from Sanskrit and reshaped by sound change. It comes from \emph{vikrīyate}, \textquotedblleft{}is sold\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 11642). CDIAL notes that the Marathi verb moved from \textquotedblleft{}to be sold\textquotedblright{} to \textquotedblleft{}to sell\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{शिजवणे} (shijavṇe)}{शिजवणे (shijavṇe)}]{\mr{शिजवणे} (shijavṇe) — to cook}

\label{lesson:MR-C78-shijavne}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for to sell, then the Marathi for to open.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{शिजवणे}}
\textbf{\mr{शिजवणे}} — \emph{shijavṇe} — \textquotedblleft{}to cook\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{शिजवणे}} (\emph{shijavṇe}) is the \textquotedblleft{}make\textquotedblright{} form of Marathi \emph{śijṇẽ}, \textquotedblleft{}to be cooked by boiling\textquotedblright{}. CDIAL lists that verb under Sanskrit \emph{sidhyati}, \textquotedblleft{}succeeds, is well cooked\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13408), and also, as another possibility, under a reconstructed \emph{*śrīyate}, \textquotedblleft{}is cooked\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 12712).
\end{cousinweb}
